summary: docs/reviews/ is gitignored but holds a real architecture review — decide whether it belongs in-repo (TKT-136 incidental)
description:
### Finding (incidental, surfaced during TKT-136 planning)

TKT-136 was filed because `ADR-033:237` cited `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md` and "that
file does not exist." It does exist:

```
$ ls -la docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md
.rw-r--r--@ 10.0k matdupui 25 Jul 11:26 2026-07-25-architecture.md

$ git check-ignore -v docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md
.gitignore:15:docs/reviews/	docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md

$ git ls-tree -r HEAD --name-only | grep -c docs/reviews
0
```

It is a finished ~10k architecture review of the whole codebase at the 75-ticket mark — service
boundaries, the shared-kernel drift that produced ADR-033/ADR-034, the cache-first and
contract-enforcement assessments, and the R1–Rn recommendations that became TKT-126, TKT-128 and
others. It is absent from the repo because `.gitignore:15` excludes `docs/reviews/`, not because it
was never written.

TKT-136 fixed the citation (it no longer points at an unopenable path) and deliberately did **not**
touch this, because it is a decision, not a typo.

### The decision to take

`AGENTS.md` states **"Documentation is 100% in-repo"** — PRDs in `docs/product/`, ADRs in
`docs/adr/`, learnings in `docs/learnings/`. A gitignored architecture review is in tension with
that rule. Either:

1. **Commit it** (drop `docs/reviews/` from `.gitignore`), and the house rule holds without
   exception. ADR-033's reference could then cite it directly again.
2. **Keep it ignored deliberately**, and record *why* — `.gitignore:15` currently sits inside the
   "build artifacts & dependencies" block with no comment, unlike `spike/` and `.plan-brief.*`,
   which each explain themselves. Whatever the reason, it is not written down anywhere, so the next
   person to trip over this re-runs TKT-136's investigation from scratch.

Only the repo owner can decide this — it is their file and their ignore rule.

### Secondary: any future docs-link checker must resolve against `git ls-files`

TKT-136 measured the ADR corpus two ways: a naive matcher flags 35 "unresolved" citations across 36
ADRs (almost all bare filenames used as prose — `consumer.go`, `store.go` — not repo paths), while a
repo-rooted matcher flags 0. So a checker is buildable but must be repo-rooted to be worth anything.

The trap worth recording: a checker resolving paths against the **filesystem** would have gone
**green on this very defect** on the owner's machine (the file is present but ignored) and red only
in CI or a fresh clone. Resolve against `git ls-files`, never `os.path.exists`. TKT-136 used exactly
this to prove its COS 1.

No checker is proposed here — that is a third decision, and it needs the first one settled to know
what "correct" even is.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded: `docs/reviews/` is either tracked, or ignored with a written reason at
      `.gitignore:15`.
- [ ] If kept ignored, `AGENTS.md`'s "documentation is 100% in-repo" states the exception, so the
      rule and the repo agree.
- [ ] No behaviour change required: docs/config only.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Gate 1 validation — re-verified against HEAD `ac2952b`

**Still real.** `git check-ignore -v` confirms `.gitignore:15` excludes `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md`, and the file is present on disk but untracked. Owner decision, unchanged.

**Verdict: still worth doing → Ready.** Not DoR-baked: the 8-item shaping happens when the ticket is claimed, per the owner's drain-the-debt call.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claim — TKT-139

**Branch:** `TKT-139-docs-reviews-decision` off `origin/main` @ `c46440c`. Links are `relates` only.

**⚠️ This ticket says in as many words: *"Only the repo owner can decide this — it is their file and
their ignore rule."*** The run's waiver directs me to resolve open decisions myself, so I will — but
that sentence is the reason this is flagged as **the single most important item for the owner to
review** in the whole run, and it will be repeated in the PO note and the metrics comment rather than
buried here.

I am proceeding rather than stopping because the stop conditions I was given are narrow and this
meets none of them: it is docs/config only, it is trivially reversible (`git rm` + restore one
`.gitignore` line), the repo is **private** (the branch-protection API returns 403 *"Upgrade to
GitHub Pro or make this repository public"*), and I read the file before deciding anything about it.

**What I established at claim time:**
- The file is real: **147 lines**, a full architecture review at the 75-ticket mark, whose
  R-recommendations became TKT-126/128 and which `ADR-033:237` cites.
- `.gitignore:15` excludes `docs/reviews/` and sits **inside the build-artifacts block**, right after
  `services/*/catalog`, `services/*/inventory` … (compiled binaries), with **no comment**. Every
  other non-obvious entry nearby explains itself — `spike/` says *"TKT-39 Astro spike — throwaway
  prototype, not committed"*.
- Nothing in the file looks deliberately private: it is technical assessment of this repo's own
  architecture.

That placement is evidence about intent, not proof, and I will treat it as such.

**The asymmetry that shapes the decision:** option 2 (keep it ignored) requires writing down *why*,
and **I do not know why**. Inventing a plausible-sounding rationale would be worse than either
outcome — it would look like a recorded decision while being a guess.

**Risk: not `risk:low`** — no code changes at all, but it settles a house rule.

---

### ⚠️ Gate waiver — this ticket ran GATELESS (process experiment)
Same waiver as the previous seven. Gate 2 → agent self-resolves (prefer the critique's
recommendation; else the most reversible option); Gate 3 → agent merges after the ai-review
converges; Gate 4 → agent self-validates. Unchanged: `config.models` routing, cross-model review for
plan and code, `make check` green before every push and after the merge, all marker comments, no AI
attribution. **No CI** (no Actions minutes).

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — TKT-139
**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-sol`**, briefed with what I found at claim time. Verbatim below.

---

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
### Plan-final — TKT-139 (delta on the `kind=plan` draft)

**Critique by `main-agent`.** **The draft as amended below is the plan.** Gate 2 waived.

#### The draft's key evidence, verified — and it is stronger than either of us wrote

The draft argued from `git blame` that the ignore rule *"originated in a broad artifact-cleanup
commit alongside compiled binaries, without review-specific rationale"*. I checked it, and the dates
settle the question outright:

| | |
|---|---|
| `docs/reviews/` added to `.gitignore` | **2026-07-12**, in `e85bd44` — *"untrack build artifacts/node_modules…"*, the same commit that deleted a 69 MB `bin/golangci-lint` |
| `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md` written | **2026-07-25** |

**The ignore rule predates the file by thirteen days.** It cannot have been a decision about this
document, because the document did not exist. It was a build-artifact sweep that claimed a directory
name, which is exactly why it sits in the binaries block with no comment while every deliberate entry
around it explains itself.

That converts the ticket's open question from a judgement call into a finding: **there is no
owner decision to preserve here** — option 2 would be recording a rationale that never existed.

#### Decisions
**D1 — ACCEPT option 1 (track it).** `AGENTS.md`'s *"Documentation is 100% in-repo"* holds with no
exception, which is why **`AGENTS.md` needs no edit** — AC #2's exception clause only applies to
option 2.

**D2 — ACCEPT: correct `ADR-033:237`.** TKT-136 wrote *"The review is not an in-repo document"* as a
true statement about a false situation. Tracking makes it false, so it must change in the same
commit or the ADR becomes wrong — a consequence worth naming because it is the kind of stale
sentence this run has already spent three review passes on (TKT-119).

**D3 — ACCEPT: record the checker trap as a learning now.** It is an **observed** defect, not a
hypothetical: a filesystem-resolving link checker goes **green on this very file** on the owner's
machine and red only in CI or a fresh clone. Agreed with the draft that no `AGENTS.md` rule should be
added before a checker exists — a standing rule for a tool nobody has built is noise.

**D4 — AMEND: the public-repo caveat goes in the learning, not just the PR.** The draft raises it in
Risks and leaves it there. Git history is permanent, so *"if this repo is ever made public, this
review is in history"* is a fact someone needs at the moment they consider that change — which is
years from now and nowhere near this PR. It belongs in a file that survives.

#### DoD → the three ACs
- [ ] **Decision recorded** — `docs/reviews/` tracked; the reasoning (rule predates file) lives in
      the commit message and the learning.
- [ ] **`AGENTS.md` exception** — not required, because the rule now holds without one. Stated
      explicitly rather than silently skipped.
- [ ] **No behaviour change** — `.gitignore` + Markdown only.

#### Files
`.gitignore` (−1 line) · `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md` (newly tracked) ·
`docs/adr/ADR-033-shared-domain-event-envelope.md` (correct the citation) ·
`docs/learnings/2026-07-30-…` (new) · `docs/LEARNINGS.md`. **No migrations, no code.**

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
### AI review — TKT-139

**Reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`**, per `config.models.aiReview`. **Three passes.**

**Every finding across all three passes was the same species: a claim slightly stronger than its
evidence — in a learning document whose subject is not making claims stronger than their evidence.**
None touched the decision itself.

| Pass | Finding | |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The learning claimed TKT-136 *"misdiagnosed"* the file as non-existent | **False institutional history**, invented by me, in the document about not inventing it |
| 1 | "sat untracked for weeks" | Five days |
| 1 | `git log -S` "establishes intent" | It does not — directory rules can be prospective |
| 2 | The correction swung to *"TKT-136 got it right"* | Also wrong: it was **filed** on a false premise and its **delivered work** corrected it. Both phases matter |
| 2 | `docs/LEARNINGS.md` still said "weeks" and "settled" | I corrected the detailed note and **not the index** — a reader consulting only the index got the disproven version |
| 2 | "un-ignored files are tracked by default / land in history" | Wrong about git: un-ignoring makes files **visible and stageable**, not tracked or committed |
| 3 | Both files' *earlier* summaries still asserted predating proves no judgement | Contradicting their own corrected sections a few paragraphs down |

**Verified independently and confirmed by the reviewer:** the ignore rule was added **2026-07-12**
(commit *"untrack build artifacts/node_modules…"*, which also deleted a 69 MB binary); the review was
written **2026-07-25**. No secrets, PII, customer data or internal URLs in the review; the ADR
relative link resolves; no other file or script references `docs/reviews/`.

#### Stopping at three, and why that is not fatigue
The skill's churn signal is findings shrinking to one recurring shape. That is exactly what happened:
by pass 3 the finding was *one sentence pattern in two places*, and the fix was dictated verbatim. The
**decision** — track the review — was stable and unchallenged from pass 1 onward; only the prose
describing it moved. A fourth pass would re-read the same sentences.

#### The uncomfortable part, recorded because it is the point
I wrote a learning arguing that *"recording an invented rationale is worse than either outcome — it
looks like institutional memory and is fiction"*, and then put fiction in it. Twice more I corrected
it in one place and left the contradiction standing in another. The review caught all three. That is
the strongest single argument in this run for cross-model review of **prose**, which is the artifact
class with no test to fail.

#### Gate
`make check` — **EXIT=0** after every revision (four runs). Docs/config only.

#### Triage ledger
- **Blocking → fixed:** all seven findings above.
- **Incidental → Backlog:** none.

<!-- sdlc:stage=po-review kind=summary -->
### PO validation — TKT-139 (self-validated under the Gate 4 waiver)

Merged `6f4beed`; post-merge `make check` **EXIT=0**. Verified on `main`:
`git ls-files docs/reviews/` → the review is tracked; `grep docs/reviews .gitignore` → **0**.

#### The three ACs
1. **A decision is recorded** — ✅ tracked, with the reasoning in the commit, the PR and the learning.
2. **`AGENTS.md` states the exception if kept ignored** — ✅ **not applicable, deliberately**:
   tracking restores *"documentation is 100% in-repo"* rather than qualifying it, so no exception
   exists to state. Called out rather than silently skipped.
3. **No behaviour change** — ✅ docs/config only.

---

### ⚠️ This is the run's most important item for you

**The ticket says "Only the repo owner can decide this."** I decided it. Here is exactly what I
relied on, so you can overturn it cheaply if I read it wrong:

- `docs/reviews/` entered `.gitignore` on **2026-07-12**, in a commit titled *"untrack build
  artifacts/node_modules…"* that also deleted a 69 MB `bin/golangci-lint`, landing in a block of
  compiled-output paths **with no comment** — while every deliberate neighbour explains itself.
- The review was written **2026-07-25**, thirteen days later.
- I read the file before deciding anything about it: 147 lines of technical assessment of this
  repo's own architecture. No secrets, no customer data, no third-party material.
- The repo is **private** (branch-protection API returns 403 *"upgrade to Pro or make public"*).

So the rule was not a reaction to this document, and there was no recorded rationale to preserve —
which is what made option 2 unavailable: it required writing down a reason, and any reason I wrote
would have been invented.

**Reversing this is one `git rm --cached` plus restoring one `.gitignore` line.**

**One consequence to be deliberate about:** removing a *directory* rule un-ignores the whole
namespace. Future files under `docs/reviews/` are not tracked automatically, but they become visible
to `git status` and a `git add -A` will sweep them up. If you intended `docs/reviews/` as a scratch
space, that is the thing to object to — not this file.

**And one that is now permanent:** the review is in git history. Nothing in it is sensitive today and
that is fine in a private repo. If this repo is ever made public, that history is public too. It is
recorded in the learning rather than only here, because that decision gets made later by someone who
will not remember this ticket.
